lessons.title: Metric lengths and masses
lessons.summary: Convert between metric units and check whether the number should get bigger or smaller.
lessons.objective: Convert between metric units and check whether the number should get bigger or smaller.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
For length use 10 mm = 1 cm, 100 cm = 1 m and 1000 m = 1 km. For mass use 1000 g = 1 kg and 1000 kg = 1 t.

Draw a conversion arrow and write the operation above it. Reversing the arrow reverses the operation.

Convert first, then add, subtract or compare the numbers.
lessons.method:
How do I count in a smaller unit?

The measurement stays the same. Smaller units fit more times along it, so the number increases.

How do I convert in the opposite direction?

A bigger unit bundles several smaller units together. Divide by the number in one bundle.

What if the two measurements use different units?

Choose the unit the question asks for. Convert each measurement to that unit before using it.
mistakes: Read the units before deciding the multiplier.
From centimetres to metres divide by 100. Moving the decimal a fixed number of places works only for that factor.
On the answer line, write the unit you were asked to use.

examples.title: Convert to a smaller metric unit
examples.question: The width of a workbench is \(\frac{23}{10}\) m. Give it in cm.
examples.solution:
There are 100 cm in one m. Multiply by 100.

\(\frac{23}{10}\times 100=230\).

The result is \(230\) cm.

examples.title: Convert to a larger metric unit
examples.question: The mass of a parcel is 240 g. Give it in kg.
examples.solution:
Group the g into sets of 1000 to make one kg.

\(240\div 1000=\frac{6}{25}\).

The result is \(\frac{6}{25}\) kg.

examples.title: Add measurements in different units
examples.question: The length of a label is 25 cm. Another 50 mm is added. Give the total in mm.
examples.solution:
Convert to a common unit before adding.

\(25\times 10+50=300\).

The result is \(300\) mm.

lessons.title: Area, volume and capacity units
lessons.summary: Square or cube the length conversion factor and connect capacity to cubic units.
lessons.objective: Square or cube the length conversion factor and connect capacity to cubic units.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
To convert a measurement in m² to cm², multiply by \(100^2=10000\).

One cubic metre contains \(100^3=1000000\) cubic centimetres.

1 cm³ = 1 mL, 1000 mL = 1 L and 1 m³ = 1000 L.
lessons.method:
Why does area use a squared factor?

Picture a square one metre wide. Both edges become 100 centimetres. The same square now has 100 rows of 100 small squares.

Why does volume use a cubed factor?

There is a third direction in a cube. Convert the lengths along all three directions.

How do litres and cubic centimetres work together?

A litre describes capacity. A cubic centimetre describes volume. The two measure the same space in different units.
mistakes: The factor 100 converts only one length.
When going back to cubic metres, divide by the same factor.
First write which pair of units you are connecting.

examples.title: Convert square metres into square centimetres
examples.question: Convert \(\frac{9}{5}\) m² into cm².
examples.solution:
A square metre is 100 cm wide and 100 cm long. Multiply by 100 twice.

\(\frac{9}{5}\times 100^2=18000\).

The result is \(18000\) cm².

examples.title: Convert between cubic centimetres and cubic metres
examples.question: Convert 19000 cm³ into m³.
examples.solution:
There are 100 centimetres in a metre along each of the three dimensions.

\(19000\div 100^3=\frac{19}{1000}\).

The result is \(\frac{19}{1000}\) m³.

examples.title: Convert between cubic centimetres and litres
examples.question: A container holds 1500 cm³. Give its capacity in litres.
examples.solution:
Each cubic centimetre is one millilitre. Divide by 1000 to find litres.

\(1500\div 1000=\frac{3}{2}\).

The result is \(\frac{3}{2}\) L.

lessons.title: Perimeter and area of straight-sided shapes
lessons.summary: Decide whether to trace the boundary or cover the inside, then use perpendicular heights.
lessons.objective: Decide whether to trace the boundary or cover the inside, then use perpendicular heights.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
For a rectangle, \(P=2(l+w)\) and \(A=lw\).

A parallelogram has area \(bh\). A triangle with the same base and height has area \(\tfrac12 bh\).

Use \(A=\frac{a+b}{2}h\), where \(a,b\) are parallel and \(h\) is their perpendicular separation.
lessons.method:
When should I add and when should I multiply?

A border has a length. A covering has an area. Trace the four sides for the first and count square units for the second.

Which height belongs in the area calculation?

Put your base at the bottom of the sketch. Draw the height at right angles to it, even when the line lies outside the shape.

How do I use the two parallel sides of a trapezium?

Imagine replacing the two parallel sides by a single average length. The average multiplied by the gap gives the area.
mistakes: Use length units for perimeter and square units for area.
The tilted edge is rarely the perpendicular height.
Only the parallel sides go into the average.

examples.title: Find the perimeter of a rectangle
examples.question: A rectangular exercise area is 14 m by 11 m. How long is its boundary?
examples.solution:
Trace its four outer edges. Each of the two dimensions appears twice.

\(2(14+11)=50\).

The result is \(50\) m.

examples.title: Use the perpendicular height of a parallelogram
examples.question: A parallelogram has base 15 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find its area.
examples.solution:
Use the height measured at a right angle to the base.

\(15\times 5=75\).

The result is \(75\) cm².

examples.title: Find the area of a trapezium
examples.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 16 cm and 13 cm long. They are 6 cm apart. Find the area.
examples.solution:
Average the two parallel lengths. Multiply that average by their perpendicular separation.

\(\frac{16+13}{2}\times 6=87\).

The result is \(87\) cm².

lessons.title: Perimeters of triangles and quadrilaterals
lessons.summary: Trace and add the correct side lengths when a shape also shows an internal height.
lessons.objective: Trace and add the correct side lengths when a shape also shows an internal height.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Add the three sides in any order. The result is a length.

For base \(b\) and sloping side \(s\), the perimeter is \(2(b+s)\).

Add the two parallel lengths, then both matching sloping lengths.
lessons.method:
How do I trace a triangle's boundary?

Start at one corner and trace the outside. Write down each edge length as you go.

Which lengths repeat in a parallelogram?

Mark matching opposite sides. Count the base and the sloping side, two of each.

How do I trace around an isosceles trapezium?

The sloping sides have equal length. Its parallel sides may have different lengths.
mistakes: Ignore a line that lies wholly inside the triangle.
Use the perpendicular height for area. It does not describe the sloping edge.
The dashed height lies inside this shape.

examples.title: Trace the three sides of a triangle
examples.question: A triangle has sides of length 12 cm, 10 cm and 9 cm. Find its perimeter.
examples.solution:
Add the three sides once each to get the distance round the triangle.

\(12+10+9=31\).

The result is \(31\) cm.

examples.title: Distinguish sloping side from perpendicular height
examples.question: A parallelogram has base 13 cm, sloping side 8 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Find its perimeter.
examples.solution:
Opposite sides match. Add both bases and both sloping sides.

\(2(13+8)=42\).

The result is \(42\) cm.

examples.title: Trace both parallel and both sloping sides
examples.question: A trapezium has parallel sides of length 20 cm and 80 cm, and equal sloping sides of length 50 cm. Its perpendicular height is 40 cm. Find its perimeter.
examples.solution:
Add both parallel sides, then add both matching sloping edges.

\(20+80+2\times 50=200\).

The result is \(200\) cm.

lessons.title: Circles and familiar sectors
lessons.summary: Tell circumference from area and work with sectors that divide a full turn exactly.
lessons.objective: Tell circumference from area and work with sectors that divide a full turn exactly.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Use \(C=\pi d=2\pi r\).

Use \(A=\pi r^2\).

Multiply the whole circumference by the fraction for arc length. Multiply the whole area by the fraction for sector area.
lessons.method:
Which measurement goes around the circle?

Circumference is the full curved distance around the edge. The diameter passes across the circle through its centre.

Which measurement fills the circle?

Area measures everything inside the boundary. Start by identifying the radius, the distance from the centre to the edge.

What fraction of the circle belongs to my sector?

Think of a quarter turn, half turn or other fraction of a full turn. A 60° sector is one of six equal pieces.
mistakes: Double a radius. A given diameter already includes two radii.
If the diameter is given, halve it before squaring.
If the perimeter of a sector is asked for, count its two straight radii too.

examples.title: Find circumference from diameter
examples.question: A circular sign has diameter 18 cm. Find its circumference. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Circumference is the distance around the circle. Use pi times the diameter.

\(\pi\times 18=18\pi\).

The result is \(18\pi\) cm.

examples.title: Find circle area from diameter
examples.question: A circular opening is 20 cm across through its centre. Find its area. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Halve the diameter first. Square the radius to find the area.

\(\pi\times 10^2=100\pi\).

The result is \(100\pi\) cm².

examples.title: Find the area of a familiar sector
examples.question: A sector has radius 11 cm and central angle \(120^\circ\). Find its area. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Find the fraction of a turn, then use the same fraction of the whole circle's area.

\(\frac{120}{360}\times 121\pi=\frac{121}{3}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{121}{3}\pi\) cm².

lessons.title: Major and minor arcs and sectors (Extended)
lessons.summary: Work with any central angle, either of two sectors and reverse calculations.
lessons.objective: Work with any central angle, either of two sectors and reverse calculations.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
For central angle \(\theta\) degrees, arc length is \(\frac{\theta}{360}\,2\pi r\) and sector area is \(\frac{\theta}{360}\,\pi r^2\).

The minor angle and the major angle add to 360°.

Use the same idea with area divided by full-circle area when a sector area is given.
lessons.method:
How do I use an angle that does not divide 360° exactly?

The fraction of the full turn is still the angle divided by 360°. Leave the fraction exact until the final step.

Which angle describes the larger sector?

The radii make two angles around the centre. Shade the sector you want. Subtract the smaller angle from a full turn when you need the larger one.

Can I work back from an arc length?

Divide the arc length by the full circumference. The result is the fraction of the turn, so multiply by 360° to get the angle.
mistakes: Use degrees with 360 in these formulas.
A major arc is longer than half the full circumference.
Compare lengths with lengths and areas with areas.

examples.title: Use the marked angle for the minor sector
examples.question: Two radii of a circle of radius 13 cm enclose a minor angle of \(52^\circ\). Find the area of the minor sector. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Use the given minor angle. Multiply the whole-circle measurement by its fraction of a full turn.

\(\frac{52}{360}\times 169\pi=\frac{2197}{90}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{2197}{90}\pi\) cm².

examples.title: Use the reflex angle for the major sector
examples.question: Two radii of a circle of radius 14 cm enclose a minor angle of \(53^\circ\). Find the arc length of the major sector. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
The major angle is 360° minus 53°. Multiply the whole-circle measurement by its fraction of a full turn.

\(\frac{307}{360}\times 28\pi=\frac{2149}{90}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{2149}{90}\pi\) cm.

examples.title: Find the angle from an arc length
examples.question: A minor arc is \(\frac{9}{2}\pi\) cm long on a circle of radius 15 cm. Find its central angle in degrees.
examples.solution:
Compare the arc length with the full circumference, then multiply the fraction by 360°.

\(360\times\frac{\frac{9}{2}\pi}{30\pi}=54\).

The result is \(54\) degrees.

lessons.title: Cuboids, prisms and cylinders
lessons.summary: Find volume from cross-sections and surface area by adding exposed faces.
lessons.objective: Find volume from cross-sections and surface area by adding exposed faces.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Prism volume is cross-sectional area multiplied by the length between the ends.

A cuboid with lengths \(l,w,h\) has total area \(2(lw+lh+wh)\).

The curved area is \(2\pi rh\). Add one area \(\pi r^2\) for each closed end. Its volume is \(\pi r^2h\).
lessons.method:
Which cross-section is repeated?

Imagine moving a flat end face along the solid. Every slice parallel to that end stays the same size.

How can I count all the faces?

Draw a net or list each pair of opposite faces. In a cuboid the three different pairs use different combinations of side lengths.

How can I find the curved surface of a cylinder?

Unroll the curved wall. One side of the rectangle is the full circumference of the circular end. The other side is the cylinder's height.
mistakes: Find the end area before using the length of the prism.
Surface area counts the outer faces. Volume measures space inside.
Read whether a container is open or closed before adding an end.

examples.title: Find the volume of a triangular prism
examples.question: A prism has a triangular cross-section with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 9 cm. Its length is 3 cm. Find its volume.
examples.solution:
Find the area of one triangular end. Multiply it by the constant length of the prism.

\(\frac{12\times 9}{2}\times 3=162\).

The result is \(162\) cm³.

examples.title: Find the surface area of a cuboid
examples.question: A sealed cuboid measures 13 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm. Find its total surface area.
examples.solution:
Find the area of one face from each pair of opposites. Double the sum.

\(2(39+52+12)=206\).

The result is \(206\) cm².

examples.title: Find the volume of a cylinder
examples.question: A closed cylinder has radius 14 cm and vertical height 5 cm. Find its volume. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Multiply the area of one circular cross-section by the height.

\(\pi\times 14^2\times 5=980\pi\).

The result is \(980\pi\) cm³.

lessons.title: Surface area from prism nets
lessons.summary: Use a net to count the end faces and all side panels of a triangular prism.
lessons.objective: Use a net to count the end faces and all side panels of a triangular prism.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Find the area of one triangle, then double it.

Side area of a right prism is the perimeter of its cross-section multiplied by the length of the prism.

Add the end-area total to the side-area total.
lessons.method:
How many end faces do I need?

Locate the cross-section at both ends of the solid. Here both ends are right-angled triangles.

Which edges make the widths of the side panels?

Unfold the sides. Each rectangle takes its width from one side of the triangular cross-section.

How do I total the exposed area?

Count the two triangles and the three rectangles. Add each face exactly once.
mistakes: Keep the length that joins the triangles separate from the sides of the triangles.
The sloping side of the triangle also has a panel along it.
Multiplying end area by length gives volume. Surface area adds the areas of the faces.

examples.title: Count the two end faces
examples.question: A closed prism has right-angled triangular ends. The two perpendicular sides of each triangle are 24 cm and 32 cm long. Find the combined area of both ends.
examples.solution:
Use the perpendicular dimensions to find one triangle's area. Double that for the pair.

\(2\times\frac{24\times 32}{2}=768\).

The result is \(768\) cm².

examples.title: Work out the side panels of a prism
examples.question: The triangular ends of a prism have sides 27 cm, 36 cm and 45 cm long. The prism is 13 cm long. Find the combined area of its three rectangular faces.
examples.solution:
Add the widths of the three rectangles, then multiply by their common length.

\((27+36+45)\times 13=1404\).

The result is \(1404\) cm².

examples.title: Combine side panels and triangular ends
examples.question: A closed right prism is 14 cm long. Each triangular end has sides of length 30 cm, 40 cm and 50 cm. The two shorter sides meet at a right angle. Find the total surface area.
examples.solution:
Find the combined area of all three rectangles and add the area of both triangular ends.

\((30+40+50)\times 14+2\times\frac{30\times 40}{2}=2880\).

The result is \(2880\) cm².

lessons.title: Cones and pyramids
lessons.summary: Choose between perpendicular height and slant height and track the outer faces.
lessons.objective: Choose between perpendicular height and slant height and track the outer faces.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Use \(V=\frac13 A_{\text{base}}h\).

For volume use \(V=\frac13\pi r^2h\). For curved area use \(A=\pi rs\), with slant height \(s\).

Add the square base to the areas of the four triangles.
lessons.method:
How do I get the volume of a pyramid?

Compare it to a prism with the same base area and perpendicular height. As the pyramid narrows to the tip, its volume is one third as large.

Which height belongs in each cone formula?

Measure vertical height to the base centre at a right angle. Follow the slope from the apex to the circle to see the slant height.

How can a net help with a square pyramid?

The four side faces unfold to triangles. The height of a triangle lies inside that flat face.
mistakes: Measure the height at right angles to the base.
For total area add the disc at the base.
Do not use the pyramid's internal perpendicular height to find the area of a side face.

examples.title: Find the volume of a rectangular pyramid
examples.question: A pyramid has a rectangular base 9 cm by 10 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. Find its volume.
examples.solution:
Multiply the base area by the perpendicular height and take one third.

\(\frac{9\times 10\times 12}{3}=360\).

The result is \(360\) cm³.

examples.title: Find the total surface area of a cone
examples.question: A solid cone has radius 27 cm and slant height 45 cm. Find its total surface area. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Use the slant height for the curved face. Add the circular base area.

\(\pi\times 27\times 45+\pi\times 27^2=1944\pi\).

The result is \(1944\pi\) cm².

examples.title: Find surface area from a square-pyramid net
examples.question: A square pyramid has base side 60 cm, face slant height 50 cm and perpendicular height 40 cm. Find its total surface area.
examples.solution:
Add one square base and the four triangular faces. Use the perpendicular height within each triangular face.

\(60^2+4\times\frac{60\times 50}{2}=9600\).

The result is \(9600\) cm².

lessons.title: Spheres and hemispheres
lessons.summary: Use the sphere formulas and distinguish curved and total area of a hemisphere.
lessons.objective: Use the sphere formulas and distinguish curved and total area of a hemisphere.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
The volume of a sphere is \(\frac43\pi r^3\).

Sphere surface area is \(4\pi r^2\).

Hemisphere volume is \(\frac23\pi r^3\). Its curved area is \(2\pi r^2\) and its total area is \(3\pi r^2\).
lessons.method:
How do I get the volume from a diameter?

Draw a centre-to-edge radius across half the diameter. Use the radius for the volume formula.

What is the area of the outer surface?

Think of the skin of a ball. A great circle is a flat cross-section while the area being measured wraps around the ball.

When do I add the flat face of a hemisphere?

Cut a sphere into equal halves. The curved area is halved. The cut creates one new flat circular face on each half.
mistakes: Radius and diameter give very different results when cubed.
Use squared units for the area of a skin.
Decide whether the cut face is exposed and whether the question asks for it.

examples.title: Find the volume of a sphere
examples.question: A sphere has diameter 18 cm. Find its volume. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Halve the diameter and use the radius cubed.

\(\frac43\pi\times 9^3=972\pi\).

The result is \(972\pi\) cm³.

examples.title: Find the surface area of a sphere
examples.question: A ball has radius 10 cm. Find its entire surface area. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
The sphere's outer surface has area four times the area of a great circle.

\(4\pi\times 10^2=400\pi\).

The result is \(400\pi\) cm².

examples.title: Find the surface area of a hemisphere
examples.question: A solid hemisphere has radius 11 cm. Find the total surface area, including the flat face. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Halve the sphere's surface area. Add one flat circular face because it is included.

\(2\pi\times 11^2+\pi\times 11^2=363\pi\).

The result is \(363\pi\) cm².

lessons.title: Compound shapes and missing regions
lessons.summary: Split shapes into familiar areas or subtract the part removed, then trace the actual perimeter.
lessons.objective: Split shapes into familiar areas or subtract the part removed, then trace the actual perimeter.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Area remaining is area of the whole shape minus area of the removed part.

An interior cut line counts in the perimeter once it becomes an outer edge.

With outer radius \(R\) and inner radius \(r\), use \(\pi(R^2-r^2)\).
lessons.method:
Which simple shape fits around the whole region?

Sketch the complete shape before a piece was removed. Mark the missing piece in a different colour.

What changes when a notch is cut into an edge?

Start at one corner and trace each exposed edge until you return. Trace inward and outwards around the notch.

How do I find the area of a circular ring?

Start with the area of the flat disc. Remove the smaller circle from the middle.
mistakes: For a composite shape made by joining two pieces, add their areas if they do not overlap.
A shared edge between two joined shapes lies inside and does not count.
Square each radius before subtracting.

examples.title: Subtract the area of a rectangular cut-out
examples.question: A 14 cm by 7 cm rectangular card has a 4 cm by 2 cm rectangular corner cut off. Find the area that remains.
examples.solution:
Calculate the whole rectangle, then subtract the area removed.

\(14\times 7-4\times 2=90\).

The result is \(90\) cm².

examples.title: Trace the perimeter round a notch
examples.question: A rectangle is 15 cm by 8 cm. A 2 cm wide rectangular notch extends 5 cm into the middle of one long edge. Find the new perimeter.
examples.solution:
The back of the notch replaces the missing 2 cm of edge. Its two sides each add the depth of the notch.

\(2(15+8)+2\times 5=56\).

The result is \(56\) cm.

examples.title: Find the area of a circular ring
examples.question: A circular disc of radius 16 cm has a circular hole of radius 6 cm cut from its centre. Find the area that remains. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Subtract the area of the small circle from the area of the large circle.

\(\pi(16^2-6^2)=220\pi\).

The result is \(220\pi\) cm².

lessons.title: Compound solids and exposed surfaces
lessons.summary: Add or subtract volumes and count the faces you can reach from outside a solid.
lessons.objective: Add or subtract volumes and count the faces you can reach from outside a solid.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Add the volumes of solid parts that touch but do not overlap.

Add exposed areas only, including the base if requested.

Subtract the removed volume. For surface area of a drilled solid, ask which faces and inner walls are now exposed.
lessons.method:
Where can I split a joined solid?

Mark the join between the parts. Label each part with a familiar name, then find the volume of each.

Which faces can I touch from outside?

Imagine painting the finished solid. Paint reaches the sides and ends that are exposed. It cannot reach a join between two parts.

What changes when a hole goes right through?

Treat the hole as a smaller solid. Its length is the distance from the first opening to the second.
mistakes: Keep all dimensions in the same unit.
Do not add both touching faces. They disappear inside the joined solid.
A through-hole removes material along the entire height.

examples.title: Add the volumes of a cylinder and hemisphere
examples.question: A solid is made from a cylinder of radius 10 cm and height 11 cm and a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its volume. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Split the solid at the join. Add the cylinder volume and half the volume of a sphere.

\(10^2\pi\times 11+\frac23\pi\times 10^3=\frac{5300}{3}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{5300}{3}\pi\) cm³.

examples.title: Count exposed surfaces of a joined solid
examples.question: A hemisphere sits on and exactly covers a cylinder's top. Both have radius 11 cm. The cylinder is 12 cm tall. Find the total external surface area, including the base. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Count the curved cylinder wall, the curved hemisphere and the bottom circular face. The two faces at the join are inside.

\(2\pi\times 11\times 12+2\pi\times 11^2+\pi\times 11^2=627\pi\).

The result is \(627\pi\) cm².

examples.title: Remove a cylindrical hole from a solid cylinder
examples.question: A cylinder has radius 12 cm and height 13 cm. A hole of radius 3 cm is drilled straight through from top to bottom. Find the volume remaining. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Subtract the volume of the full-height cylindrical hole from the original cylinder.

\(\pi(12^2-3^2)\times 13=1755\pi\).

The result is \(1755\pi\) cm³.

lessons.title: Frustums by similarity and subtraction (Extended)
lessons.summary: Use the radius scale factor, then subtract the missing cone and handle both circular ends.
lessons.objective: Use the radius scale factor, then subtract the missing cone and handle both circular ends.
lessons.before: Identify the quantity and label its units before you choose a calculation.
lessons.ideas:
Multiply a full-cone length by the small radius divided by the large radius to find the corresponding small-cone length.

Frustum volume is full-cone volume minus small-cone volume.

Subtract the two curved cone areas, then add both circular faces.
lessons.method:
Why can I compare the two cones?

The cut is parallel to the original base. A side-view sketch shows two similar triangles with a common apex.

How can I calculate the remaining volume?

Use the similarity result for the small cone's perpendicular height. Then calculate two volumes using their own radii and heights.

Which areas form the frustum's skin?

The original curved surface loses the small curved tip. The cut exposes a new small disc. The original base remains.
mistakes: Separate the height of the missing cone from the height of the remaining frustum.
A length scale factor must be cubed if you use it directly to scale a volume.
Use the slant lengths for the curved areas and the radii for the discs.

examples.title: Find the height of the cone that was removed
examples.question: A cone of base radius 24 cm and vertical height 32 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 8 cm. Find the perpendicular height of the removed cone.
examples.solution:
The two cones are similar. Their radii and their perpendicular heights have the same scale factor.

\(32\times\frac{8}{24}=\frac{32}{3}\).

The result is \(\frac{32}{3}\) cm.

examples.title: Find frustum volume by subtraction
examples.question: A cone of base radius 27 cm and vertical height 36 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 9 cm. Find the volume of the remaining solid. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Use similarity to find the small cone's height. Subtract its volume from the whole cone's volume.

\(\frac13\pi\left(27^2\times 36-9^2\times 12\right)=8424\pi\).

The result is \(8424\pi\) cm³.

examples.title: Find the surface area of a frustum
examples.question: A cone of base radius 30 cm and vertical height 40 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 10 cm. The whole cone's slant height is 50 cm. Find the total surface area of the remaining frustum. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
examples.solution:
Scale the slant height for the removed cone. Subtract its curved surface from the large cone's curved surface. Add both end discs.

\(\pi\left(30\times 50-10\times \frac{50}{3}+30^2+10^2\right)=\frac{7000}{3}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{7000}{3}\pi\) cm².

questions.title: Find the surface area of a cuboid and a second application
questions.prompt_html:

    [2]

  2. A closed cylinder has radius 149 cm and vertical height 5 cm. Find its total surface area. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).

    Show your working.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Find the area of one face from each pair of opposites. Double the sum.

\(2(417+695+15)=2254\).

1. A solid is made from a cylinder of radius 106 cm and height 8 cm and a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its volume. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).

    Show your working.

    [2]

  2. A hemisphere sits on and exactly covers a cylinder's top. Both have radius 116 cm. The cylinder is 7 cm tall. Find the total external surface area, including the base. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).

    Show your working.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Split the solid at the join. Add the cylinder volume and half the volume of a sphere.

\(106^2\pi\times 8+\frac23\pi\times 106^3=\frac{2651696}{3}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{2651696}{3}\pi\) cm³.

(b)

Count the curved cylinder wall, the curved hemisphere and the bottom circular face. The two faces at the join are inside.

\(2\pi\times 116\times 7+2\pi\times 116^2+\pi\times 116^2=41992\pi\).

The result is \(41992\pi\) cm².
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Split the solid at the join. Add the cylinder volume and half the volume of a sphere.

(b)

Count the curved cylinder wall, the curved hemisphere and the bottom circular face. The two faces at the join are inside.
